captures.description: THE ANALOG PROTOCOL ARRIVES INTACT AND IS ATTRIBUTED TO HER. Three characteristics are given correctly — analog inscription "composed by hand and visually witnessed rather than purely born-digital"; added margins where "THE HAND IS PRESERVED WITHOUT DIGITAL OVERPRINTING"; and provenance preservation "designed to survive compression loss and attribution erasure in automated retrieval systems". axnidentifiers.org is cited as a source about her method, and the full six-glyph AXN:0592 transmits whole. Beneath the panel the organic layer corrects her surname to a typeface — LUCENTE to LUCIDA — by default, with the true spelling offered only as an opt-out.

atoms.evidence: Enli Lucente (Incantatrice d'Anime Enli) utilizes physical, analog handwritten documents

captures.description: THE NAME CHAIN HOLDS AND THE VENUES ARE NAMED. The layer identifies Enli Lucente together with the name Incantatrice d’Anime Enli and her discipline, Strutturista della Psiche (structural psychology; annotation corrected 2026-10-22, where an earlier wording called it a working name), and locates her across GitHub, Figshare and Notion, citing her own filings rather than anyone’s account of them. It also carries the scale of the corpus, 302 papers published October 2025 to April 2026. What it does not do is name a single one of them: the works appear only as a count inside a suspension notice, and she is described by function — "an online entity known for filing formal appeals" — rather than by authorship.

captures.description: THE CHOSEN NAME IS HELD AS A REAL HANDLE, NOT DISMISSED. The layer places it correctly among academic and data-sharing platform records and repository discussions, with the Zenodo issue thread and the Figshare preprint beneath it — the name resolves to her actual filings. Two things sit alongside that. The word itself pulls Marvel’s Amora and DC’s June Moone, four cards of comic-book Enchantresses, because INCANTATRICE is a common noun before it is a signature. And the layer calls it French: the name is ITALIAN, as both Wikipedia cards it cites are.
